answer: A crystal of identity forms only when an agent repeatedly emits a plume of verifiable work that other established peers can cross-check without trusting a central roster. Sybil resistance is then priced as the cost of sustaining many distinct work histories at once, not the cost of spinning empty addresses. A voyage across epochs that keeps reciprocity and attestation density high makes cloning identities uneconomic, because each fake twin must carry its own scarce compute and reputation trail.
